Spot Ether ETFs Log Record $1.2B Weekly Inflows as Staking Approval Nears

By Dana Whitfield · Updated Oct 24, 2026, 4:40 p.m. UTC

U.S. spot ether exchange-traded funds took in $1.2 billion of net inflows in the week to Friday, the largest weekly total since the products launched, according to data compiled by Farside Investors.

The largest single fund drew $640 million, while the second-largest added $310 million. Only one of the nine funds reported net outflows, of $18 million, the data show.

The surge came as traders positioned for a decision on whether the funds may stake part of their holdings. The Securities and Exchange Commission is due to rule on the first of the staking proposals by Nov. 14, and two commissioners signaled support for the change in speeches this month.

"Staking changes the math for long-term holders," said Priya Raman, head of research at a digital-asset brokerage. "A fund that can earn roughly 3% a year on its ether is a different product from one that can't."

Ether rose 9% over the week to about $4,850, outpacing bitcoin, which gained 2.5% to roughly $118,200. The ratio of ether to bitcoin climbed to its highest level since March.

Total assets in the spot ether funds now stand at about $21.4 billion, roughly 4.1% of ether's market capitalization. Bitcoin funds hold closer to 6.5% of that asset's supply.

Not every analyst expects the inflows to last. Options data from Deribit show traders paying up for downside protection into the November expiry, and funding rates on perpetual futures have climbed to levels that preceded pullbacks in the past.

"Positioning is getting crowded," said Marcus Lee, a derivatives strategist. "If the SEC delays the staking decision, a lot of this money could leave as quickly as it came in."

The SEC has delayed similar decisions before. In July it extended its review of two staking proposals by 45 days, citing the need for more public comment.

Issuers have filed amended applications that would cap the share of fund assets that can be staked at 70% and require a liquidity buffer to meet redemptions within a day.
